recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is recommended; future changes to the migrated profile definitions or CRMI-specific explanatory text should be handled in the CRMI source that now owns them.
issue_request: FHIR-37959 is an Applied/Persuasive Vocab issue for R6 requesting removal of the Shareable, Publishable, Computable, and Executable profiles from the core FHIR specification, with ongoing maintenance in the Canonical Resource Management Infrastructure IG and unchanged profile URIs.
initial_application: Commit 3958dd1e7c2fd73ad1e94c66f8d0884df55695d5 applied the issue by removing ValueSet profile StructureDefinitions and CodeSystem, ConceptMap, and ValueSet implementation-guide references and profile introduction files. Commit 8c199a9c87a4339854475fec053caa6519a6ba07 then removed remaining CodeSystem, ConceptMap, and NamingSystem profile StructureDefinitions plus metadata/profile references.
additional_context: May 2025 joint TI/CDS/CQI minutes record that FHIR-37959 was reopened and resolved to keep these profiles in CRMI rather than THO. The linked UP-634 THO proposal was withdrawn, FHIR-48827 was retracted as a duplicate, FHIR-47807's request to keep ValueSet profiles in core was retracted, and later CRMI issues FHIR-52711 and FHIR-52719 updated the external profile URLs and explanatory text to align with FHIR-37959.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because current source/fhir.ini has no active profile entries for the migrated terminology profiles, current resource implementation guides have no StructureDefinition references to those profiles, and the old profile StructureDefinition files are absent. Build-scope pattern and module text already points applications to the CRMI profiles.

related_jiras.note: Broader request to decide whether TI profiles should move out of core was retracted as duplicative of FHIR-37959.
Request to keep the ValueSet profiles in core was Resolved - No Change/Retracted after agreement that they should not remain in core.
CRMI issue updated migrated terminology profile URLs to retain the core-defined canonical URLs.
CRMI issue updated explanatory text to say the profiles remain in CRMI while retaining base specification URLs.
THO migration proposal was withdrawn after the May 2025 WGM decision to keep the profiles in CRMI.
